text: The CDM conditions NameOrIdChoice and NaturalPersonChoice are enforced by the ported type's #validate(); the part of them the table cannot carry is R1

comments.text: R1 and A1 only pin down the surname-or-identifier reading you attribute to NameOrIdChoice. If NaturalPersonChoice constrains anything beyond that (or constrains it differently — e.g. a different disjunction or an additional branch), nothing in the spec states it and nothing tests it. Could you confirm NaturalPersonChoice reduces to the same surname-or-identifier rule, or specify its remaining part as its own requirement/criterion?

text: The entity holds personal data — names, date of birth, government-issued identifier numbers — and is treated as PII throughout.

comments.text: The Constraints section opens with "treated as PII throughout" but then marks authorization as "none apply (platform default — any signed-in user)" and lists no other PII-driven consequence. As written, the PII declaration has no operational content in this spec: any signed-in user can read and write rows containing government-issued identifier numbers. If that is the firm's deliberate decision for this register, it may be worth one sentence saying so ("PII-labelling only; no narrower access than the platform default"); if the firm's standing rules impose anything for PII entities (narrower roles, retention, export restrictions), those are currently unstated.
